# 1 Clement Chapter 41 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 41 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_041_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 41

**41:1** Each of us, brothers, in his own rank, must give thanks to God with a clear conscience, not transgressing the prescribed rule of his own ministry, but acting with all reverence.

**41:2** Not in every place, brothers, are the continual offerings presented, or the free-will offerings, or those for sins and transgressions, but only in Jerusalem; and even there not in every spot, but before the sanctuary at the altar, after the offering has been inspected by the high priest and the ministers aforementioned.

**41:3** Those therefore who do anything contrary to what is fitting to his will receive death as the penalty.

**41:4** You see, brothers, how much greater the knowledge we have been given, the greater the danger we are exposed to.

---

## Translator's Note

Chapter 41 is the application of ch. 40's OT template to the Christian situation. The argument is: (1) Even Israel's worship was geographically and procedurally restricted — only Jerusalem, only the designated altar, only through the proper priests (v. 2); (2) deviation brought death (v. 3); (3) Christians, having received even greater knowledge and responsibility, face even greater accountability (v. 4). Clement's present-tense description of temple worship (v. 2) has puzzled scholars: was the temple still standing? More likely Clement writes from scriptural knowledge or uses the present for vivid effect. The "knowledge we have been given" (v. 4) refers to the full Christian revelation, which makes disorder in the church all the more inexcusable.

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus translation, balancing literalness and clarity.*
